analysis.connectionCountingScope: Two explicit verified DynamoDB TLS dials, one per operation reused for all four phases. The separate SDK STS guard transport was not connection-instrumented and is not included.
observations: Every batch of 20 signed requests was fully written to its operation-specific verified TLS HTTP/1.1 connection before any application response read. Each batch returned 20 complete HTTP/1.1 responses with distinct native request IDs.

ListBackups initially returned five successes then 15 throttles. The immediate second batch returned one success and 19 throttles. Both two-second and ten-second idle periods were followed by five successes then 15 throttles.

DescribeBackup initially returned 12 BackupNotFoundException responses then eight throttles. The immediate second batch returned three BackupNotFoundException responses and 17 throttles. Both recovery batches returned 12 BackupNotFoundException responses and eight throttles, including a non-throttle response at position 15 after throttles at positions 12-14.

BackupNotFoundException is a modeled HTTP 400 error, not an API success; it is the observed non-throttle outcome for the syntactically valid nonexistent backup ARN. ThrottlingException also returned HTTP 400. ListBackups successes returned HTTP 200 with empty BackupSummaries.

The 20-request write spans were 36.383-112.781 microseconds. ListBackups batches completed 0.199-0.269 seconds after write start; DescribeBackup batches completed 0.229-0.419 seconds after write start.
limitations: Client Write completion measures local submission, not AWS packet arrival or admission time. Requests were offered without per-request response waits, but the server may serialize or otherwise delay processing.

Initial and recovered non-throttle counts are observed batch outcomes, not exact instantaneous bucket capacities. Processing-time refill may affect results; later non-throttle response positions are retained rather than normalized away.
Identical request bodies within an operation mean response-to-request mapping is positional under HTTP/1.1, not independently proven with unique per-request inputs.
One account, one region, one run and one TLS connection per operation do not establish account-global scope, fleet topology, cross-connection sharing, or a universal private bucket/refill algorithm.
Idle intervals describe this probe only; unrelated AWS activity was not controlled.

experiment.endpointPolicy: Removed all AWS_ENDPOINT_URL* environment entries; AWS_IGNORE_CONFIGURED_ENDPOINT_URLS=true; explicit native regional STS endpoint and DynamoDB TLS host
experiment.responseMapping: HTTP/1.1 response position assumed to correspond to request position; identical inputs within an operation cannot independently demonstrate backend response ordering
experiment.retryer: No retries; AWS NopRetryer for STS, raw single Write per request and sequential ReadResponse for DynamoDB
